name: Blue Team
summary: Defensive tooling for intrusion detection, hardening and system auditing
description: Tools for defenders and system owners: network and host intrusion detection, file-integrity and rootkit checks, log analysis, security auditing and benchmarking, sandboxing and firewalls. All are open-source packages from Debian; they help you watch, harden and audit systems you administer.

tools.name: Suricata
tools.summary: Network intrusion detection, prevention and security monitoring

tools.name: CrowdSec
tools.summary: Behaviour-based intrusion detection with collaborative blocklists
tools.notes: Larger download; the engine parses logs and feeds decisions to a firewall bouncer you install separately.

tools.name: Fail2ban
tools.summary: Ban hosts that show repeated authentication failures

tools.name: AIDE
tools.summary: Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment for file integrity

tools.name: Rootkit Hunter
tools.summary: Scan for rootkits, backdoors and local exploits

tools.name: chkrootkit
tools.summary: Check a system or mounted image for signs of a rootkit

tools.name: Lynis
tools.summary: Security auditing and hardening tool for Unix systems

tools.name: Linux Audit daemon
tools.summary: Record security-relevant events against the kernel audit subsystem

tools.name: ClamAV
tools.summary: Open-source antivirus engine and command-line scanner

tools.name: YARA
tools.summary: Match files and processes against pattern rules for malware triage

tools.name: OpenSCAP scanner
tools.summary: Evaluate systems against SCAP security policy (oscap)

tools.name: debsecan
tools.summary: List known CVEs affecting the installed Debian packages

tools.name: arpwatch
tools.summary: Monitor Ethernet/IP address pairings and alert on changes

tools.name: sshguard
tools.summary: Block brute-force attacks against SSH and other services

tools.name: psad
tools.summary: Detect port scans and suspicious traffic from firewall logs

tools.name: lnav
tools.summary: Navigate and query log files from an interactive terminal UI

tools.name: Firejail
tools.summary: Restrict an application's environment with a security sandbox

tools.name: USBGuard
tools.summary: Allow or block USB devices by policy to limit attack surface

tools.name: OpenSnitch
tools.summary: Interactive application firewall that prompts on outbound connections
tools.notes: This is the GUI that shows prompts and statistics; it pulls in the opensnitch daemon that enforces the rules.

tools.name: Wireshark
tools.summary: Graphical network protocol analyser
tools.notes: Capturing needs permission to the interface; Debian's dpkg-reconfigure wireshark-common sets up the 'wireshark' group so you need not run it as root.

external.name: Zeek
external.summary: Network security monitor that turns traffic into rich logs
external.license: BSD-3-Clause (open source), not currently packaged in Debian trixie.

why.text: Zeek is free software but is not in Debian trixie; the project maintains its own repositories and source releases.

how.text: Install from the official Zeek binary packages for Debian, or build from the source release, per the Zeek documentation.

external.name: Wazuh
external.summary: Host-based intrusion detection and security monitoring platform
external.license: GPL-2.0 (open source), distributed from Wazuh's own repositories.

why.text: Wazuh's agent and manager are not in Debian; the project maintains its own APT repository and release packages.

how.text: Add the official Wazuh APT repository and install the agent or manager following the Wazuh installation guide.

external.name: Velociraptor
external.summary: Endpoint visibility and digital-forensics collection at scale
external.license: AGPL-3.0 (open source), released as prebuilt binaries by Rapid7.

why.text: Velociraptor is distributed as single-file release binaries and is not packaged in Debian.

how.text: Download the official release binary for Linux from the Velociraptor releases page and verify its signature.

external.name: Elastic Stack (ELK)
external.summary: Search, log aggregation and visualization for security analytics
external.license: Mixed; recent versions under the Elastic License / SSPL, which are not DFSG-free.

why.text: Elasticsearch and Kibana are shipped under Elastic's own licences and are not in Debian main; Elastic provides packages from its repositories.

how.text: Install from Elastic's official APT repository, or run the maintained container images, per the Elastic documentation.
